cards.title: What is AgentCore?
cards.hook: AWS's agentic platform: build, deploy, and operate agents at scale — any framework, any model.

back.lead: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a fully managed platform for running AI agents in production. You bring the agent code; AgentCore supplies infrastructure, session isolation, memory, tool connectivity, identity, governance, and monitoring — with no servers to manage.

kv.v: Works with any framework (Strands, LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex) and any model — Bedrock-hosted or not (incl. Anthropic API).
Preview Jul 16 2025 → generally available Oct 13 2025, with VPC, PrivateLink, CloudFormation, and tagging support.
Sits in AWS's agent infrastructure layer alongside Bedrock (models), Nova, and Strands Agents (framework).

back.hookline: It is not a framework and not a model — it's the production substrate underneath whichever framework and model you choose.

cards.title: Modular by design
cards.hook: Nine-plus composable services. Use one, some, or all — nothing forces a full-stack commitment.

back.lead: AgentCore is a kit of independent services: Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, plus the newer Policy, Evaluations, and Registry. Each has its own API and pricing; they interoperate but never require each other.

kv.v: E.g. run agents on your own compute but use only Gateway for tool access, or only Memory for context.
All services support VPC connectivity and PrivateLink for private-network access.
You can adopt incrementally — wrap an existing local agent loop with one AgentCore service at a time.

back.hookline: Think 'LEGO for agent infrastructure', not a monolithic agent product.

cards.title: MCP & A2A support
cards.hook: Standard protocols glue it together: MCP for tools, Agent-to-Agent for inter-agent calls.

back.lead: AgentCore leans on open protocols rather than proprietary interfaces. Gateway speaks Model Context Protocol so any MCP-compatible agent can discover and call tools; Runtime added Agent-to-Agent (A2A) support at GA so agents can invoke each other directly.

kv.v: Gateway exposes tools over MCP and can also proxy to your existing MCP servers.
Enables multi-agent systems: delegation, sub-agents, and agent-as-tool patterns across Runtime deployments.
An open-source AgentCore MCP Server lets coding assistants (Claude Code, Kiro, Q Developer) drive AgentCore itself.

back.hookline: Protocol-first design is why 'any framework' is credible — the contract is MCP/A2A, not an SDK lock-in.

cards.title: AgentCore Runtime
cards.hook: Serverless agent hosting: one isolated microVM per session, executions up to 8 hours.

back.lead: Runtime hosts your agent (or tool) code. Every session gets a dedicated microVM with full session isolation, so one user's context can never leak into another's. It auto-scales, needs zero infrastructure management, and supports long-running work up to eight hours.

kv.v: Container-based (ECR) or direct code deployment (artifacts in S3). Framework-agnostic entry point.
MicroVM per session — filesystem, memory, and compute are per-user, then destroyed.
8-hour execution window is industry-leading; built for deep research, pipelines, and headless loops.
Pay only for active CPU/memory consumption — not for time spent waiting on LLM or API I/O.

back.hookline: Runtime = 'Lambda for agents', but with sessions, statefulness, and hours-long lifetimes.

cards.title: AgentCore Memory
cards.hook: Managed short-term and long-term memory so agents remember across turns — and across sessions.

back.lead: Memory gives agents managed recall. Short-term memory captures raw session events (the conversation as it happens). Long-term memory runs extraction strategies over those events to distill durable knowledge that persists across sessions.

kv.v: Built-in: semantic facts, summaries, and user preferences. A self-managed strategy (GA) lets you run your own extraction/consolidation pipeline.
Added at re:Invent 2025: per-user episodic memory for personal preferences (seat choice, budget caps, style).
Memory streaming (2026) reduces the lag between an event happening and it becoming retrievable.
{{slot:memory_price}}

back.hookline: Short-term = the transcript. Long-term = what a good assistant would write in their notebook afterwards.

memory_price.rendered: Consumption-based; short-term events billed per volume (launched around $0.25 per 1,000 events).

cards.title: AgentCore Gateway
cards.hook: Turns your APIs, Lambda functions, and MCP servers into one governed tool endpoint for agents.

back.lead: Gateway is the tool integration layer. It transforms existing REST APIs (OpenAPI specs), Lambda functions, and AWS services into MCP-compatible tools, and can also front your existing MCP servers — giving agents a single secure endpoint for tool discovery and invocation.

kv.v: Wrap what you already have; Gateway handles protocol translation, credentials, and error normalization.
Supports both IAM (SigV4) and OAuth authorization for agent→tool calls.
Runtime tool discovery + semantic search means agents aren't handed hundreds of tools at once, which degrades tool selection.
Gateway is where Policy intercepts every tool call (see AC-11).

back.hookline: Gateway is the choke point — one endpoint for all tools means one place to authenticate, observe, and enforce policy.

cards.title: AgentCore Identity
cards.hook: Auth built for non-human identities: agents acting as themselves or on a user's behalf.

back.lead: Identity handles authentication, authorization, and credential management for agents. It covers inbound auth (who may invoke the agent) and outbound auth (what the agent may access), with a secure token vault for refresh tokens.

kv.v: Integrates with Cognito, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta and other IdPs — no user migration or rebuilt auth flows.
OAuth 2.0 flows, API keys, and AWS SigV4.
Agents can act on behalf of users with pre-authorized consent, or autonomously with their own identity — to services like GitHub, Slack, Salesforce.
Identity-aware authorization and vault storage for refresh tokens.

back.hookline: The key question Identity answers: 'the agent called an API — as whom, and who said it could?'

cards.title: Code Interpreter
cards.hook: A sandboxed environment where agents write and execute code — Python, JavaScript, TypeScript.

back.lead: Code Interpreter gives agents an isolated sandbox to write, run, and debug code. This dramatically improves accuracy on math, data analysis, and file transformation tasks, because the agent computes answers instead of guessing them.

kv.v: VM-level sandboxing keeps generated code away from your systems.
Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript at launch.
Per-second, based on active CPU/memory — you don't pay while the sandbox idles waiting on the model.
Data analysis, chart generation, file conversion, validation logic, agent 'self-checks'.

back.hookline: LLMs approximate; code computes. Give the agent an interpreter and its numeric answers become verifiable.

cards.title: Browser tool
cards.hook: A managed cloud browser so agents can navigate sites, fill forms, and finish web tasks.

back.lead: The Browser tool provides fast, secure, cloud-hosted browser sessions that agents drive to interact with real web applications — navigation, form-filling, and multi-step web workflows — with sub-second latency and session isolation.

kv.v: VM-level isolation per session plus audit-friendly recording of what the agent did.
Browser profiles persist cookies/local storage between sessions (stored in S3, billed at S3 rates from Apr 2026) — so agents stay logged in.
Sites without APIs, legacy portals, and end-to-end tasks where the web UI is the only interface.

back.hookline: API when you can, browser when you must — this is the 'when you must' escape hatch, fully managed.

cards.title: Observability
cards.hook: OpenTelemetry-based tracing of every reasoning step, tool call, and token an agent spends.

back.lead: Observability gives step-by-step visibility into agent execution: reasoning traces, tool invocations, latency, errors, and token/cost metrics — end to end across all AgentCore services, surfaced through CloudWatch and OTEL-compatible backends.

kv.v: Inspect full session trajectories with metadata tagging, custom scoring, and debug filters.
Built on OpenTelemetry, so traces flow into your existing observability stack, not a walled garden.
Traditional APM sees latency and errors; agent observability must also answer 'did it pick the right tool and why?'

back.hookline: You can't govern or improve what you can't see — Observability is the raw data feed for Evaluations.

cards.title: Policy
cards.hook: Hard, enforced boundaries on agent actions — defined in natural language, enforced at the Gateway.

back.lead: Policy lets you define what agents may and may not do — in natural language — and enforces it outside the model's reasoning loop. A policy engine attached to a Gateway intercepts every tool call before it executes and permits or denies it.

kv.v: Run a policy in log-only mode to validate it against live traffic, then flip to enforce.
'Never modify financial records directly'; 'Require human approval for refunds over $X'; 'Only read data for the logged-in user'.
These are infrastructure-level constraints, not system-prompt suggestions — prompt injection can't talk its way past them.
Preview at re:Invent (Dec 2 2025) → GA March 2026.

back.hookline: The auditor-friendly distinction: 'we hope the agent behaves' vs 'we can prove it can't misbehave'.

faces.back:
AC-18 · DETAILECONOMICS

Pricing model

Every AgentCore service is pay-as-you-go with no upfront commitment or minimums. The headline economic feature: Runtime, Browser, and Code Interpreter bill per-second on active CPU/memory only — and agentic workloads typically spend 30–70% of wall-clock time in I/O wait.

Compute
Per-second CPU + memory for Runtime / Browser / Code Interpreter (active consumption only).
Gateway
Per tool invocation (launched around $0.005 per 1,000 calls) plus request charges.
Memory
Billed on event/data volume; short and long term priced separately.
Storage
Direct-code deploys billed at S3 rates; container deploys at ECR rates; browser profiles at S3 rates.
Memory hookAn agent that 'thinks' for 60s but computes for 6s bills roughly like 6s — that's the whole pitch vs. always-on containers.
